options: Energy of an object's motion or position
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Energy of an object's motion or position". Mechanical energy is the energy of an object's motion or position.

mechanical.q: Mechanical energy is the energy of an object's motion or its ____.
mechanical.hint: The answer is "position". Mechanical energy comes from motion or position.

options: Mechanical energy is the same as light energy
Mechanical energy can be kinetic or potential
Mechanical energy is only found in machines
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Mechanical energy can be kinetic or potential". Motion energy (kinetic) and position energy (potential) are both mechanical.

mechanical.q: Which term means 'the energy of an object's motion or position'?
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Mechanical energy". That is the meaning of mechanical energy.

mechanical.q: Mechanical energy is made of which two kinds of energy?
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Kinetic and potential". Kinetic is motion and potential is position.

mechanical.q: Which is an example of mechanical energy?
options: The warmth of a cup of cocoa
mechanical.hint: The answer is "A swinging playground swing". A moving swing has energy of motion.

mechanical.q: Which is NOT an example of mechanical energy?
options: A ball flying through the air
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Sunlight shining through a window". Sunlight is light energy, not motion or position of an object.

mechanical.q: Which shows mechanical energy because of where it is (its position)?
options: A rock sitting at the top of a hill
mechanical.hint: The answer is "A rock sitting at the top of a hill". A raised rock has stored energy from its position.

mechanical.q: Which group shows only examples of mechanical energy?
options: Spinning top, falling leaf, rolling cart
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Spinning top, falling leaf, rolling cart". All of those things are moving.

mechanical.q: Pick the one that belongs with 'mechanical energy'.
options: A kite flying in the wind
A charged battery in a drawer
mechanical.hint: The answer is "A kite flying in the wind". A flying kite is moving, so it has energy of motion.

mechanical.q: Mia puts her backpack on a high shelf, where it stays. What energy does it have because it is up high?
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Potential energy". A raised object has stored (potential) energy because of gravity.

mechanical.q: Leo kicks a soccer ball and it rolls across the field. Which part of mechanical energy does the rolling ball show?
options: Chemical, because it is stored in food
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Kinetic, because it is moving". Moving objects have kinetic energy.

mechanical.q: At a science fair, Ava lets a toy car roll down a ramp. Which energy is she showing?
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Mechanical energy". The car's height and motion are mechanical energy.

mechanical.q: A roller coaster car sits at the top of a big hill, then zooms down. What happens to its energy?
options: Position energy changes to motion energy
Motion energy changes to light energy
mechanical.hint: The answer is "Position energy changes to motion energy". Potential energy from height changes into kinetic energy.

mechanical.q: Your class wants a quick demo of mechanical energy. What would you use?
options: A flashlight shining on a wall
A ball bouncing on the floor
mechanical.hint: The answer is "A ball bouncing on the floor". A bouncing ball has motion and position energy.

potential.hint: The answer is "Stored energy". Potential energy is stored energy.

potential.q: A raised object has stored energy because of ____.
potential.hint: The answer is "gravity". Gravity gives a raised object stored energy.

options: Potential energy can change into kinetic energy
Potential energy only comes from sunlight
Potential energy can never change form
potential.hint: The answer is "Potential energy can change into kinetic energy". Stored energy can change into motion energy.

potential.q: Which word means 'stored energy' like a raised ball or a stretched spring has?
potential.hint: The answer is "Potential". Potential energy is stored energy.

potential.q: What can you do to a spring to store potential energy in it?
potential.hint: The answer is "Squeeze it". Squeezing (compressing) a spring stores potential energy.

potential.q: Which has potential energy because it is raised up?
options: A book on a high shelf
A song playing on the radio
potential.hint: The answer is "A book on a high shelf". A raised object stores energy because of gravity.

potential.q: Which is an example of potential energy from stretching?
potential.hint: The answer is "A stretched rubber band". Stretching a rubber band stores potential energy.

potential.q: Which one is NOT storing potential energy?
options: A kid sitting at the top of a slide
potential.hint: The answer is "Sunlight shining on the grass". Sunlight is light energy, not stored energy from height or stretching.

potential.q: Which group shows only stored potential energy?
options: Rolling ball, spinning top, running dog
Pulled-back bow, raised hammer, squished spring
Pulled-back bow, ringing bell, lamp light
potential.hint: The answer is "Pulled-back bow, raised hammer, squished spring". Raised, stretched or squeezed things store potential energy.

potential.q: Pick the one that belongs with 'potential energy'.
options: A drum making a loud boom
A light shining in the dark
A diver standing on a high board
potential.hint: The answer is "A diver standing on a high board". The diver is up high, so the diver has stored energy.

potential.q: Sam pulls back the rubber band on a slingshot and holds it still. What does the stretched band have?
potential.hint: The answer is "Stored potential energy". Stretching a rubber band stores potential energy.

potential.q: Sam lets go and the rubber band snaps forward. What energy change happens?
options: Sound energy changes to potential energy
Potential energy changes to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy changes to light energy
potential.hint: The answer is "Potential energy changes to kinetic energy". The stored energy changes into motion energy.

potential.q: Two balls that are the same sit on two shelves. Which has more stored energy from gravity?
options: The ball on the higher shelf
The ball on the lower shelf
potential.hint: The answer is "The ball on the higher shelf". The higher an object is raised, the more energy it stores.

potential.q: Ben has a toy that jumps when its spring is pushed down and let go. What should he do first to store energy in it?
potential.hint: The answer is "Push the spring down". Squeezing (compressing) a spring stores potential energy.

potential.q: Why does a ball you hold up high start to fall when you let go?
options: Gravity pulls it and stored energy becomes motion
The ball runs out of energy
potential.hint: The answer is "Gravity pulls it and stored energy becomes motion". Stored energy from height changes into kinetic energy as it falls.

options: Energy stored in food, fuels and batteries
chemical.hint: The answer is "Energy stored in food, fuels and batteries". Chemical energy is stored in food, fuels and batteries.

chemical.q: Chemical energy is stored in food, fuels like ____, and batteries.
chemical.hint: The answer is "gasoline". Gasoline is a fuel that stores chemical energy.

options: Chemical energy can never change form
Chemical energy is only found in the sun
Chemical energy can change into a form that does work
chemical.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy can change into a form that does work". Stored chemical energy can change into a form that does work.

chemical.q: Which term means 'energy stored in food, fuels and batteries'?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy". That is the meaning of chemical energy.

chemical.q: What kind of energy does a battery store?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy". A battery stores chemical energy.

chemical.q: Which one has stored chemical energy?
chemical.hint: The answer is "A banana". Food like a banana stores chemical energy.

chemical.q: Which is NOT an example of chemical energy?
chemical.hint: The answer is "A rainbow". A rainbow is light, not stored energy in food, fuel or a battery.

chemical.q: Which group all store chemical energy?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Apple, gasoline, battery". Food, fuel and batteries all store chemical energy.

chemical.q: Pick the one that belongs with 'chemical energy'.
chemical.hint: The answer is "Firewood". Wood is a fuel, so it stores chemical energy.

chemical.q: Which thing in your kitchen stores chemical energy?
options: The light from the ceiling lamp
The beep of the oven timer
chemical.hint: The answer is "A box of cereal". Cereal is food, and food stores chemical energy.

chemical.q: You eat breakfast, then run at recess. What energy from the food helps your body move?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy". Food stores chemical energy that your body changes into motion.

chemical.q: A flashlight runs on batteries. What kind of energy is stored in the batteries?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy". Batteries store chemical energy.

chemical.q: A car burns gasoline to drive. What does the gasoline's stored energy change into to make the car move?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Kinetic (motion) energy". Chemical energy in gasoline changes to kinetic energy.

chemical.q: Campers burn wood in a campfire. What does the wood's stored energy change into?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Heat and light". Burning wood changes chemical energy into heat and light.

chemical.q: Your toy robot won't move anymore. What could you replace to give it a new supply of stored energy?
chemical.hint: The answer is "Its batteries". Batteries store chemical energy the robot can use.

kinetic.hint: The answer is "The energy of motion". Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.

kinetic.q: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because it is ____.
kinetic.hint: The answer is "moving". Kinetic energy is the energy of a moving object.

options: A still rock has kinetic energy
Only cars can have kinetic energy
Anything that is moving has kinetic energy
kinetic.hint: The answer is "Anything that is moving has kinetic energy". Every moving object has kinetic energy.

kinetic.q: What is another name for kinetic energy?
kinetic.hint: The answer is "Motion energy". Kinetic energy is also called motion energy.

kinetic.q: A ball stops rolling and sits still. How much kinetic energy does it have now?
options: The same as when it was rolling
kinetic.hint: The answer is "None". Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, so a still object has none.

options: A rock sitting on the ground
kinetic.hint: The answer is "A running dog". The dog is moving, so it has kinetic energy.

kinetic.q: Which is NOT an example of kinetic energy?
options: A book resting on a desk
kinetic.hint: The answer is "A book resting on a desk". The book is not moving, so it has no kinetic energy.

kinetic.q: Which group shows only things with kinetic energy?
options: Flying bird, rolling ball, moving swing
Parked car, still rock, closed book
Flying bird, parked car, still rock
kinetic.hint: The answer is "Flying bird, rolling ball, moving swing". All of those things are moving.

kinetic.q: Pick the one that belongs with 'kinetic energy'.
options: A kid racing down the slide
A pencil lying on the floor
kinetic.hint: The answer is "A kid racing down the slide". A kid sliding down is moving, so the kid has kinetic energy.

kinetic.q: Which playground thing shows motion energy?
kinetic.hint: The answer is "A spinning merry-go-round". The spinning merry-go-round is moving.

kinetic.q: Zoe pedals her bike faster and faster. What happens to her kinetic energy?
kinetic.hint: The answer is "It goes up". The faster something moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

kinetic.q: A bowling ball rolls into the pins and they fall over. Why do the pins move?
options: The pins were pulled by sound
The ball's motion energy was passed to them
The pins made their own light energy
kinetic.hint: The answer is "The ball's motion energy was passed to them". The moving ball's kinetic energy is passed to the pins.

kinetic.q: At a science fair, Omar shows a pinwheel spinning in the wind. What energy does the spinning pinwheel have?
kinetic.hint: The answer is "Kinetic energy". A spinning pinwheel is moving, so it has kinetic energy.

kinetic.q: Ella's toy car uses a battery to zoom across the floor. What energy goes in, and what comes out to make it move?
kinetic.hint: The answer is "Chemical in, kinetic out". The battery's chemical energy changes into motion energy.

kinetic.q: Dad fills the car with gasoline and drives you to school. What energy change makes the car move?
kinetic.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy to kinetic energy". Gasoline's stored chemical energy changes to kinetic energy.

lighttravel.q: How does light travel from its source?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "Outward in all directions". Light travels outward from its source in all directions.

lighttravel.q: Light travels in a ____ line until it hits an object or moves into a new material.
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "straight". Light travels in a straight line.

options: Light always travels in curved paths
Light can pass through some objects
Light can never pass through anything
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "Light can pass through some objects". Some objects, like clear glass, let light pass through.

lighttravel.q: What three things can happen to light when it hits something?
options: It can be melted, frozen, or boiled
It can be stretched, squeezed, or rolled
It can be reflected, refracted, or absorbed
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "It can be reflected, refracted, or absorbed". Light can be reflected, refracted, or absorbed.

lighttravel.q: In science, what is a medium?
options: A material that light travels through
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "A material that light travels through". A medium is a material, like air, water or glass.

lighttravel.q: Which one can light pass through?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "A clear glass window". Clear glass lets light pass through.

lighttravel.q: Which shows that light travels in straight lines?
options: Light curving around a corner wall
A flashlight beam going straight across a dark room
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "A flashlight beam going straight across a dark room". Light travels in straight lines, so the beam is straight.

lighttravel.q: Which is a light source that sends light out in all directions?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "A lit candle". A lit candle makes light that spreads out in all directions.

lighttravel.q: Which object will NOT let light pass through?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "A cardboard box". Light cannot pass through thick cardboard.

lighttravel.q: Which group of things all let light pass through?
options: Window glass, clear water, plastic wrap
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "Window glass, clear water, plastic wrap". Clear materials let light pass through.

lighttravel.q: You hide behind a big tree while your friend shines a flashlight at it. Why can't the light reach you?
options: Light goes straight and the tree blocks it
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "Light goes straight and the tree blocks it". Light travels in a straight line until it hits an object.

lighttravel.q: A lamp sits in the middle of the room. Who can its light reach?
options: People on every side of it
Only the person in front of it
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "People on every side of it". Light travels outward in all directions.

lighttravel.q: Ms. Lee shines a flashlight through three cards with holes. The light reaches the wall only when the holes line up. What does this show?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "Light travels in straight lines". Light only gets through when the holes make a straight path.

lighttravel.q: Sunlight shines on a pond. Which of these could NOT happen to the light?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "It turns into water". Light can be reflected, refracted, or absorbed, but it does not become water.

lighttravel.q: You want sunlight to reach a plant inside a box. What should you cover the opening with?
lighttravel.hint: The answer is "Clear plastic". Light can pass through clear plastic.

reflect.hint: The answer is "To bounce off". Reflect means to bounce off.

reflect.q: We see objects because light ____ off them.
reflect.hint: The answer is "reflects". Light reflects off objects and into our eyes.

options: Flat, smooth surfaces reflect light evenly
reflect.hint: The answer is "Flat, smooth surfaces reflect light evenly". Smooth, flat surfaces like mirrors reflect light evenly.
The answer is "Reflect". Reflect means to bounce off.

reflect.q: Why can you see a book in a lit room?
options: The book makes its own light
Light bounces off the book into your eyes
Your eyes shine light onto it
reflect.hint: The answer is "Light bounces off the book into your eyes". We see objects because light reflects off them.

reflect.q: Which reflects light evenly so you see a clear picture of yourself?
reflect.hint: The answer is "A flat mirror". A flat, smooth mirror reflects light evenly.

reflect.q: Which surface would NOT give a clear reflection?
reflect.hint: The answer is "Rough, choppy water". Rough water does not reflect light evenly.

reflect.q: Which group all give clear, even reflections?
options: Mirror, still pond, smooth shiny metal
reflect.hint: The answer is "Mirror, still pond, smooth shiny metal". Flat, smooth surfaces reflect light evenly.

reflect.q: Which is an example of reflection?
options: A straw looking bent in water
A strawberry taking in blue light
Seeing your face in a mirror
reflect.hint: The answer is "Seeing your face in a mirror". Light bounces off the mirror back to your eyes.

reflect.q: Which object do we see only because light bounces off it, not because it makes its own light?
reflect.hint: The answer is "A chair". A chair makes no light; we see it because light reflects off it.

reflect.q: Jake looks into a lake on a windy day and can't see a clear picture of himself. Why?
options: Rough water does not reflect evenly
reflect.hint: The answer is "Rough water does not reflect evenly". Rough water does not reflect light evenly.

reflect.q: At night, car headlights hit a bike reflector and it shines back. What is happening?
options: The reflector makes its own light
The reflector bends light down into the road
reflect.hint: The answer is "Light bounces off the reflector". The reflector bounces the car's light back.

reflect.q: In class, Mia wants to bounce a flashlight beam onto a poster across the room. What should she use?
reflect.hint: The answer is "A flat mirror". A flat, smooth mirror reflects light evenly.

reflect.q: The lights go off in a room with no windows, and you can't see your toys. Why?
options: The toys shrink in the dark
No light is reflecting off them to your eyes
The toys disappear in the dark
reflect.hint: The answer is "No light is reflecting off them to your eyes". We see objects only when light reflects off them.

reflect.q: You shine a flashlight at a mirror. Where does most of the light go?
options: It bounces back off the mirror
It goes into the mirror and stops
reflect.hint: The answer is "It bounces back off the mirror". A mirror reflects light, which means it bounces off.

refract.hint: The answer is "To bend". Refract means light bends.

refract.q: Light ____ when it goes from air into water.
refract.hint: The answer is "slows down". Light slows down when it goes from air into water.

options: Light travels at different speeds in different materials
Light travels at the same speed in every material
refract.hint: The answer is "Light travels at different speeds in different materials". Changing speed between materials is why light bends.

refract.q: Which word means light bending as it passes between materials?
refract.hint: The answer is "Refract". Refract means to bend.

options: Only when it hits a flat mirror
When it passes from one material into another
refract.hint: The answer is "When it passes from one material into another". Light refracts when it passes between different materials.

refract.q: Which is an example of refraction?
options: A straw looks bent in a glass of water
refract.hint: The answer is "A straw looks bent in a glass of water". Light bends between water and air, so the straw looks bent.

refract.q: Which is NOT an example of refraction?
options: A magnifying glass making print look bigger
A pencil looking broken in water
refract.hint: The answer is "Light bouncing off a mirror". Bouncing off is reflection, not bending.

refract.q: Which object is made to bend light?
refract.hint: The answer is "A magnifying glass lens". A lens bends (refracts) light.

refract.q: Which group all show light bending?
options: Black shirt, dark rug, red flower
Bent-looking straw, magnifying lens, pencil in water
refract.hint: The answer is "Bent-looking straw, magnifying lens, pencil in water". Each of these bends light as it passes between materials.

refract.q: Pick the one that belongs with 'refract'.
options: A swimming pool looking less deep than it really is
refract.hint: The answer is "A swimming pool looking less deep than it really is". Light bends as it leaves the water, so the pool looks shallower.

refract.q: Ava puts a pencil in a glass of water. It looks broken at the water line. Why?
options: The water really broke the pencil
Light bends as it passes between water and air
The pencil melted in the water
refract.hint: The answer is "Light bends as it passes between water and air". Light refracts between water and air.

refract.q: Max shines a flashlight at a slant into a tank of water. What will the beam do as it enters the water?
refract.hint: The answer is "Bend". Light slows down in water and bends.

refract.q: At a science fair, Kim shows a magnifying glass making words look bigger. What is the lens doing to the light?
refract.hint: The answer is "Bending it". A lens refracts (bends) light.

refract.q: Your friend reaches for a toy on the bottom of a pool but misses. Why?
options: Light travels in curves through air
Light bends, so the toy is not exactly where it looks
The toy moves away by itself
refract.hint: The answer is "Light bends, so the toy is not exactly where it looks". Light bends as it leaves the water, which fools your eyes.

refract.q: Which would you use to show refraction to your class?
options: A clear glass of water and a straw
A flat mirror and a flashlight
refract.hint: The answer is "A clear glass of water and a straw". A straw looks bent in water because light bends.

absorb.hint: The answer is "To take in". Absorb means to take in.

absorb.q: The color we see is the color that is ____.
absorb.hint: The answer is "reflected". We see the color an object reflects.

options: Light is made of different colors
Light has no colors in it
absorb.hint: The answer is "Light is made of different colors". Light is made of different colors.
The answer is "Absorb". Absorb means to take in.

absorb.q: A red flower reflects red light. What does it do with the other colors?
absorb.hint: The answer is "Absorbs them". A red flower absorbs the other colors.

absorb.q: Which object reflects green light and absorbs the other colors?
absorb.hint: The answer is "A green leaf". We see a leaf as green because it reflects green.

absorb.q: Which is an example of light being absorbed?
options: A straw looking bent in water
A dark rug taking in sunlight
absorb.hint: The answer is "A dark rug taking in sunlight". Taking in light is absorbing.

absorb.q: A blue shirt looks blue. Which color of light does it reflect?
absorb.hint: The answer is "Blue". We see the color an object reflects, and it absorbs the other colors.

absorb.q: Which list matches each thing with the color it reflects?
options: Banana: blue, grass: red, strawberry: green
Banana: green, grass: yellow, strawberry: blue
Banana: yellow, grass: green, strawberry: red
absorb.hint: The answer is "Banana: yellow, grass: green, strawberry: red". We see the color each object reflects.

absorb.q: Red light shines on these things. Which one absorbs the red light?
absorb.hint: The answer is "Blue jeans". Blue jeans reflect blue and absorb other colors, like red.

absorb.q: Lily sees a red flower in the garden. Why does it look red?
options: It reflects red and absorbs the other colors
It makes its own red light
It absorbs red and reflects the other colors
absorb.hint: The answer is "It reflects red and absorbs the other colors". We see the color that is reflected.

absorb.q: In class, Mr. Park shines light through a prism and a rainbow appears on the wall. What does this show?
options: The prism is full of paint
Light is made of different colors
absorb.hint: The answer is "Light is made of different colors". Light is made of different colors.

absorb.q: On a sunny day, Sam wears a black shirt and Ava wears a white shirt. Whose shirt absorbs more light?
absorb.hint: The answer is "Sam's black shirt". Black takes in almost all colors of light; white reflects them.

absorb.q: A strawberry absorbs the blue and green light that hits it. Which color does it reflect to your eyes?
absorb.hint: The answer is "Red". The color we see is the color reflected.

absorb.q: A paper towel soaks up spilled milk. Which science word means this kind of 'taking in'?
absorb.hint: The answer is "Absorb". Absorb means to take in.
